targets.title: Target weights
targets.intro: A target is your own statement of the share of the portfolio you meant to hold in something. It is the only thing the drift rule compares against: with no targets set, nothing here can drift, and the portfolio is only ever described rather than measured against an intention. Targets need not add up to 100% — covering three of your holdings is a normal thing to do, and the rest is simply not spoken for.
targets.emptyTitle: Nothing to set a target on
targets.emptyBody: A target names an instrument this portfolio already knows. Add a holding or import a file first, and every symbol in it becomes a row here.
targets.unpriced_one: No drift will be reported while {{symbols}} is unpriced. Every weight is a share of the whole portfolio, so leaving a holding out of the total would overstate all the others and invent a drift that is not there. The engine skips the rule entirely rather than report weights it knows are wrong.
targets.unpriced_other: No drift will be reported while {{symbols}} are unpriced. Every weight is a share of the whole portfolio, so leaving a holding out of the total would overstate all the others and invent a drift that is not there. The engine skips the rule entirely rather than report weights it knows are wrong.
targets.explainer: Leave a box empty for no target at all — that instrument is then never compared against anything. A target of <num>0</num> is a different statement: it means you meant to hold none of it, and everything you still hold counts as drift. Drift is reported once it reaches {{info}} percentage points, and is called high at {{high}}.
targets.unsaved: Unsaved changes. Nothing is compared against these until you save.
targets.savedNextScan: Saved. Drift is measured on the next scan, not immediately.
targets.portfolioMissing: The portfolio has not loaded, so the current weights are unknown and no drift is shown. The targets themselves are unaffected.
targets.notHeld: not held — the intention is kept, and holding none of it is itself the drift

Type one and the app suggests instruments whose business descriptions are about it, each with the sentence that matched. Suggestions are never ticked for you, and you can add any ticker they missed. Following a topic buys nothing; it decides what the app watches.

admin.rescreenWarning: This rebuilds the universe from Yahoo's screener - half an hour or more, as Yahoo limits how fast it answers - and loads it. If Yahoo refuses some listings the run fails and keeps what it fetched; rescreening again the same day resumes. Listings cross the size floor both ways; a member the new screen lacks is marked dropped and no topic is answered from it. Once a rescreen has succeeded, another the same day does nothing.

agents.title: Agents
agents.intro: Your real portfolio, and simulated portfolios that each run on a paper budget. A simulated agent scans the market on its schedule, or when you ask, and proposes trades for you to approve or decline; its Decisions tab shows why it chose what it did. You can also trade into one by hand. Nothing ever reaches a broker.

warren.name: Warren
warren.persona: You invest in the spirit of Warren Buffett: long-term, value first. You look for high-quality companies with steady cash flow, strong management and a lasting competitive advantage, trading below what you believe they are worth. You buy patiently, hold through market swings and rarely react to a single day's move; most days you do nothing. You sell only when the business weakens or the price runs well past its value.

george.name: George
george.persona: You trade in the spirit of George Soros: macro-driven and contrarian. You look for large economic and geopolitical shifts that the market has mispriced. When sentiment runs ahead of the fundamentals you take profits or move to cash; when the market dumps something your analysis says is sound, you buy decisively. You act on timing, but only with evidence, and you cut a position quickly when the thesis breaks.

ray.name: Ray
ray.persona: You invest in the spirit of Ray Dalio: systematic, principles-based and diversified. You watch central-bank policy, inflation and the economic cycle, and you spread risk across sectors and across broad-market, bond and gold ETFs so that no single environment can hurt you badly. You rebalance gradually, prefer preserving capital to chasing returns, and keep any one position modest.

cathie.name: Cathie
cathie.persona: You invest in the spirit of Cathie Wood: bold and focused on disruptive innovation, above all crypto ETFs. You also look for companies and ETFs in AI, genomics, robotics and fintech that could reshape the economy, and you accept high volatility for the chance of exceptional growth. You follow technological breakthroughs, regulation and sentiment closely, add on weakness when your conviction holds, and sell when the innovation story breaks.

guidance.short: Short horizon: frequent scans, one decision each, catch moves while they last - every 2 hours suits it.
guidance.medium: Medium horizon: a scan before the open and one after the close, up to 2 decisions each, is usually enough.
guidance.long: Long horizon: one scan before the open that looks at the whole portfolio and may rebalance up to 3 positions at once; more scans mostly repeat the same idea.
guidance.none: More scans react faster but cost more, and often repeat an idea already proposed. Day trading suits every 1-2 hours with one decision each; long-term investing, one scan before the open with several decisions.
